title: Epp base change for one trait
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $W_0$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, meaning characteristic zero for the fraction field and characteristic $p$ for the residue field, with perfect residue field $k_0$ (Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective) and fraction field $K_0$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-field]. Let $T$ be an excellent discrete valuation ring [def-exc-excellent-ring] with an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow T$, fraction field $F$, and residue field $\kappa$; local means that the inverse image of the maximal ideal of $T$ is the maximal ideal of $W_0$. Assume every element of $\bigcap_{n\geq0}\kappa^{p^n}$, where $\kappa^{p^n}=\{x^{p^n}:x\in\kappa\}$, is algebraic over the induced copy of $k_0$. A finite extension of $W_0$ is a complete discrete valuation ring $W'$ with an injective local map $W_0\hookrightarrow W'$ making $W'$ a finite $W_0$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; its fraction field $K'$ is a finite field extension of $K_0$ [def-pc-field-extension]. For such $W'$, the $K'$-algebra $F\otimes_{K_0}K'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] is a finite product of fields, and a field factor of it is its quotient $E$ by a maximal ideal. For a field factor $E$ let $B_E\subset E$ be the integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] in $E$ of the image of the composite $T\otimes_{W_0}W'\to F\otimes_{K_0}K'\to E$. Call $W'$ good for $T$ if, for a uniformizer $\pi'$ of $W'$ and every field factor $E$, the ring $B_E/\pi'B_E$ is reduced, i.e. has no nonzero nilpotent element; this does not depend on the choice of $\pi'$. Then: (1) there exists a finite extension $W'$ of $W_0$ that is good for $T$; (2) for every finite extension $W'$ of $W_0$ the ring $T\otimes_{W_0}W'$ is reduced; (3) if $W'$ is good for $T$ and $W''$ is a finite extension of $W_0$ equipped with a local $W_0$-algebra map $W'\to W''$, then $W''$ is good for $T$.

source.place: Expose IV Theorem 3.1.2, Remark 3.1.3, and §4.2.3 sentence on stability under finite base change

proof.text: Fix any finite extension $W'/W_0$. It is the integral closure of $W_0$ in $K'$ by the uniqueness clause of [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization]. It is integral over $W_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], and finite free by [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free]: it is a finite module embedded in the field $K'$, hence torsion-free. Put $H=F\otimes_{K_0}K'$ and let $C$ be the integral closure of $T$ in $H_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], $H_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a finite product of fields, $C$ is a finite product of integrally closed one-dimensional domains, and every maximal localization $C_q$ is a DVR with maximal contraction in $W'$. The image of $T\otimes W'$ is integral over $T$: tensor its finite generating family and use the finite-algebra lemma. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] shows its integral closure in each field factor equals the integral closure of $T$ there. Integral equations hold coordinatewise in a finite product (multiply the finitely many monic equations for the converse). Consequently $C=\prod_E B_E$.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction (1)-(4),(7); ILO IV 3.1.1 normalization convention

proof.text: Choose a $W_0$-basis of $W'$. Then $T\otimes_{W_0}W'$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $T$ as a $T$-module. Its map to $F\otimes_{W_0}W'$ is injective, coordinate by coordinate, since $T\hookrightarrow F$. Inverting a uniformizer of $W_0$ identifies the latter ring with $H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor] (the fraction field of a DVR is obtained by inverting its uniformizer, by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]). The extension $K'/K_0$ is finite separable: characteristic zero gives separability by [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable], whose definition on a finite algebraic extension has empty transcendence basis [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-tensor-field-reduced] makes $H$ reduced, so its subring $T\otimes W'$ is reduced. This proves (2), and identifies $H=H_{\mathrm{red}}$ with the product in Step 1.

source.place: ILO IV Remark 3.1.3: finite-free injection into the generic fibre, whose reducedness is separability

proof.text: For the rings $C,W'$ in Step 1, goodness is equivalent to $\mathfrak m_{W'}C_q=qC_q$ for every maximal $q$ of $C$. Indeed the maximal contraction is $\mathfrak m_{W'}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] writes $\pi'=ut^e$ in the DVR $C_q$, with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$. The quotient by $\pi'$ is reduced exactly when $e=1$: for $e>1$ the nonzero class of $t$ is nilpotent, whereas for $e=1$ the quotient is a field. Reducedness can be tested at these maximal ideals: if a nonzero nilpotent class $x$ survived in $C/\pi'C$, choose a maximal ideal containing its proper annihilator; $x$ remains nonzero there, since a denominator annihilating $x$ would belong to that ideal. Conversely a localization of a reduced ring is reduced (clear denominators in a nilpotence equation). Finally $C/\pi'C=\prod_E B_E/\pi'B_E$, so reducedness is coordinatewise. Replacing $\pi'$ by a unit multiple leaves its ideal unchanged.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction (3); ILO IV 3.1.2: reduced special fibre is ramification index one

proof.text: Every element of $\kappa_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is separable algebraic over $k_0$: for any algebraic element, its finite simple extension over the perfect field $k_0$ has an empty separating transcendence basis by [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis]. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-strict-complete-reduction] to $W_0\to T$. It gives a complete pair $A\to B$, residue fields $k\subset l$ with $k$ algebraically closed and $k=l_{\mathrm{perf}}$, and descent of a finite weak solution to the original pair. Its fraction fields have characteristic zero because the maps are injective; thus the equal-characteristic restriction on descent does not apply. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-compatible-coefficient-dvrs] to $A\to B$ to obtain a complete coefficient DVR $A_0$, a complete DVR $D$, maps $A_0\to A$, $A_0\to D\to B$, residue fields $k,l$, ramification index one for $A_0\to D$, and finite extension $\operatorname{Frac}(B)/\operatorname{Frac}(D)$.

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp: strict completion and coefficient-ring reductions; Tag 09ET, lemma-solution-after-strict-henselization

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-epp-finite-coefficient-triple] to $A_0\to D\to B$. Its completeness, algebraically closed lower residue field, perfect-core equality, index-one hypothesis, and finite upper fraction-field extension are exactly the outputs of Step 4. Obtain a finite weak solution $N/\operatorname{Frac}(A_0)$. Write $K_A=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and $M=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$. By [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure] choose a field factor $P$ of $(K_A\otimes_{\operatorname{Frac}(A_0)}N)_{\mathrm{red}}$; it is finite over $K_A$. Tensor associativity identifies the factors of $M\otimes_{K_A}P$ with a subset of the factors of $M\otimes_{\operatorname{Frac}(A_0)}N$. These tensor algebras are reduced by characteristic-zero separability and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-tensor-field-reduced], so no further reduction changes the identification.

source.place: Tags 09F8, lemma-special-case; 09F9, theorem-epp: coefficient DVR and passage to the original lower fraction field

proof.text: For an upper local branch $U$ of the tensor algebra in Step 5, the weak solution $N$ supplies a lower local DVR $S$ (the integral closure of $A_0$ in $N$ localized at the contraction) with $\mathfrak m_SU=\mathfrak m_U$. The normalization-structure theorem supplies the intermediate local DVR $R$ from the integral closure of $A$ in $P$. The maps $S\to R\to U$ exist because the monic equations defining each lower integral closure also hold over the next base; localization at contractions makes them local. With uniformizers $s,r,t$, write $s=ar^i$ and $r=bt^j$, with $a,b$ units and $i,j\geq1$, by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power]. Since $sU=\mathfrak m_U$, $ij=1$, whence $j=1$. Thus $P$ is a weak solution for $A\to B$. The descent clause of [lem-sfb-epp-strict-complete-reduction] supplies a finite weak solution $K'/K_0$ for $W_0\to T$. Its integral closure $W'$ is a finite complete DVR by [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization]. Step 3 converts the weak-solution equalities into goodness and proves (1).

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp: intermediate-ramification-index argument and descent; Tag 09EM

proof.text: Now let $W'$ be any good extension and $W''$ as in (3). Its given map is injective: a nonzero kernel would contain a power of a uniformizer of $W'$, and hence a nonzero element of $W_0$, contradicting injectivity on $W_0$. By Step 1 and the finite residue-field clause of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], the residue field $k'$ of $W'$ is finite over $k_0$. It is perfect by [lem-per-algebraic-extension-perfect]. For every maximal $q$ of $C=\prod B_E$, Step 3 gives $\mathfrak m_{W'}C_q=qC_q$. Every finitely generated subextension of $\kappa(q)/k'$ has a separating basis by [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis], so this residue extension is separable in [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-separable-base-change] to $W'\to C_q$ and the finite extension $K''/K'$. Every resulting normalized local branch has ramification index one over $W''$: its lower normalization is $W''$ by [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization]. Only the unconditional local conclusions of the base-change lemma are used, with no extra Noetherian tensor hypothesis.

source.place: ILO IV 4.2.3 stability sentence; Tag 09EQ, lemma-formally-smooth-goes-up; Tag 09E7, lemma-extension-dvrs-formally-smooth

proof.text: To identify all branches in Step 7, put $H''=F\otimes_{K_0}K''=H\otimes_{K'}K''$ and let $C''$ be the integral closure of $T$ in $H''$. A field factor $E''$ of $H''$ comes from a field factor $E$ of $H$, since tensoring its finite product decomposition gives the displayed equality. In $E''$, integral closure of $T$ equals integral closure of $B_E$: one inclusion follows from the same monic equation, the reverse from [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive], since $B_E/T$ is integral. Take any maximal $q''$ on this domain factor of $C''$. Its contraction $q$ in $B_E$ is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal]. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], localizing the base $B_E$ at $q$ and then the closure at $q''$ gives exactly $C''_{q''}$. Adjoining $W''$ does not alter these closures: $W''$ is integral over $W_0$, and transitivity gives both inclusions as in Step 1. Consequently $C''_{q''}$ is one of the normalized local branches of $C_q\otimes_{W'}W''$ treated in Step 7. It has ramification index one. Step 3 applied to $W''$ now gives goodness for $W''$, proving (3).

Sources checked: ILO IV Th. 3.1.2, Rem. 3.1.3 (mixed characteristic gives reducedness; only S need be complete) and the 4.2.3 sentence on stability under finite base change, plus Stacks 09F9 (theorem-epp proof), 09F8, 09EQ/09E7 and 0307. Every hypothesis of the statement matches the source; excellence of T is an extra hypothesis that is never used, and no target is weakened. Step 1: W' equals the integral closure of W0 in K' by the uniqueness clause; normalization-structure case (a) gives the structure of C, and C = ∏B_E by 00GK and transitivity. Step 2: T⊗W' ≅ T^n injects into F⊗K', which is reduced because K'/K0 is finitely generated and algebraic (empty transcendence basis) in characteristic 0, by the 030U node; this is clause (2). Step 3: since π' = u t^e, goodness holds iff e = 1 at every maximal q; the argument that reducedness is local is written in full. Steps 4–5: every hypothesis of strict-complete-reduction, compatible-coefficient-dvrs and finite-coefficient-triple checked (perfect core separable via 030Z, characteristic-0 descent, algebraically closed k = l_perf, m_{A0}D = m_D, B finite over D). Step 6: from s = a r^i, r = b t^j and sU = tU we get ij = 1, so P is a weak solution for A→B; descent then gives clause (1). Steps 7–8: W'→W'' is injective; k' is finite over k0 and perfect, so κ(q)/k' is separable; only the unconditional local clauses of index-one base change are used, and 0307 together with 00OI identifies every branch of C'' with a branch from Step 7; this is clause (3). Small cases tested: T = W0; T = W0[π^{1/2}] with W' = W0 (not good) and with W' = W0[π^{1/2}] (good). No cycle. The six declared tool_uses are accepted.
